descriptive_title: Grade 1 Mathematics: Numbers — Addition and Subtraction Facts to 10, Mental Strategies to 20, Modelling to 50, and Equal Groups with Halves (B2.1–B2.5)
short_description: A 5-day Ontario Grade-1 unit on addition and subtraction (B2.1-B2.5), framed around Plus the Adding Pup and Minnie the Minus Mouse running 'The Adding Machine' classroom math lab. Fact recall to 10, mental strategies (doubles, near-doubles, make-ten), fact families, story-problem modelling, and equal-group sharing including halves all in one focused week.
long_description: Children spend a focused week becoming Junior Adding Machine Operators — recalling facts, applying mental strategies, modelling story problems, and solving equal-group shares. Day 1 'Meet the Adding Machine' anchors the +0 to +5 facts to 10 with double ten-frames and number-bond triangles, plus the commutative property (B2.1, B2.2). Day 2 'Doubles, Near-Doubles, and Make-Ten' is the mental-strategy keystone for sums to 20 with doubles dice, near-doubles bridging, and the make-ten transformation on the double ten-frame (B2.3). Day 3 'Where Did It Go? — Subtracting with Minnie' frames subtraction as missing-addend, builds fact-family triangles, and explicitly addresses the 'subtraction is the opposite' relationship to addition with the cup-hide game (B2.1, B2.2). Day 4 'Build It, Solve It' is the story-problem capstone: act out, model with two-colour counters, draw a tape diagram, and write the equation for change-add-to / change-take-from / part-part-whole problems with totals to 50 (B2.4). Day 5 'Equal Groups and Half Groups' closes with equal-group situations to 10, including the subtle case where each group is a half — fair-sharing 5 cookies between 2 friends as 2-and-a-half each (B2.5). Each lesson includes a 4000+ char expanded_walkthrough covering 3 misconceptions paired with concrete recovery moves; mid-unit and end-of-unit assessments included.
what_is_included: 5 fully-scripted lesson plans with 50-minute durations and 250 minutes of total teaching time
5 student worksheets aligned to each lesson with name/date fields and child-voice learning goals
1 mid-unit formative assessment (Mid-Unit Strategy Check-In) administered between Lessons 3 and 4

10 printable teacher manipulatives plus 3 character puppets: Plus the Pup paper-bag puppet, Minnie the Mouse paper-bag puppet, double ten-frame mat, two-colour counters label, fact family triangles (30 cards), doubles dice label, story problem cards (18 cards), paper cookies, sharing plates label, the Adding Machine anchor poster, plus stick-puppet variants of Plus, Minnie, and Doubles the Robot
1 end-of-unit reflection sheet with 5 self-assessment prompts
1 five-row summative rubric covering B2.1-B2.5 across 4 levels
1 summative-administration guide tying the rubric to Lesson 5 worksheet
Junior Adding Machine Operator certificate (one per child) for the closing ceremony
Detailed expanded walkthroughs for every lesson including the swap-then-make-ten move for sums like 5+8 and the cup-hide demo for fact-family-recall vs. count-back subtraction
Differentiation tracks built into every lesson: emerging learners, extending learners, ELL/IEP, and movement-first learners
target_buyer: Ontario Grade 1 teachers covering the B2.1-B2.5 cluster of the 2026 Grade 1 Math curriculum. Useful as a 5-day unit in late October or early November when students are ready to move from B1 number-sense to B2 operations, or as a fact-fluency review block in late winter before report-card cycle.
subject: Mathematics
pedagogical_approach: Concrete-Representational-Abstract progression across the 5 days. Real two-colour counters, double ten-frames, and paper cookies anchor every concept before any worksheet abstraction. The keystone Lesson 2 uses the swap-then-make-ten move to break the order-dependence misconception; the integration Lesson 3 uses fact-family-recall to break the count-back habit; the modelling Lesson 4 enforces the build-draw-write pipeline; the capstone Lesson 5 uses pre-cut paper cookies to break the 'fair share with leftover' K-stage answer. Differentiation is proactive (built into every lesson) rather than remedial.
